title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 2
paragraphs: When the army on its march came into Boeotia, the Thebans tried to detain Mardonius, counseling him that there was no region more suitable for him to encamp in than that one. They urged him not to advance further but to sit down there and try to subdue the whole of Greece without fighting: to overcome the Greeks by open force when they were united, as they were now in common accord, was (they said) a difficult task even for all the world combined. “But if you follow our advice,” they went on, “you will with little effort have in your power all their plans of resistance. Send money to the men who hold power in the cities; by doing this you will divide Greece into two parties, and after that you will easily subdue, with the help of your party, those who are not inclined to your side.”
